courses.label: PHYS 14
courses.title: Optics
paras: Geometrical optics, interference, diffraction and polarization. 3 lectures, 3 hours laboratory, one term.

courses.label: PHYS 15
courses.title: Modern Physics
paras: The fundamental particles of matter, assemblies of particles, nuclei and atoms, the wave-particle experiments, introductory quantum mechanics and atomic structure.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: PHYS 43
courses.title: Nuclear Physics
paras: The atom and its nucleus, radioactive decay, nuclear masses and nuclear stability, nuclear spin and moments, structure of nuclei, gramma radiation processes, alpha decay, beta decay, nuclear reactions, fission, interaction and radiation with matter, counters, particle accelerators and reactors.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: PHYS 44
courses.title: Classical Mechanics
paras: Moving frames of reference and the special theory of relativity. Relativistic particle dynamics. Rotating co-ordinate systems. Dynamics of a freely rotating rigid body. Generalized co-ordinates. Lagrange’s equations. Variational principles in mechanics. Hamiltonian formulation of mechanics. Transformation theory.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: PHYS 45
courses.title: Introductory Statistical Mechanics
paras: Review of essential classical and quantum mechanics, microcanonical, canonical and grand canonical ensembles; quantum statistical mechanics, theory of the density matrix; applications.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: PHYS 46
courses.title: Introduction to Quantum Mechanics
paras: Origins of quantum theory. Waves and particles. Wave functions and wave packets. Schroedinger’s equation. Onedimensional motion in regions of varying potential. Fourier analyses, eigenvalues and expectation values. Axiomatic foundations of quantum mechanics. Operators, Angular momentum. Central force systems; the hydrogen atom. 3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: PHYS 100
courses.title: General Physics I
paras: Newtonian mechanics, conservation laws, heat and thermodynamics, electrostatics, D.C. circuits. 3 lectures, 3 hours laboratory alternate weeks.

courses.label: PHYS 131
courses.title: Mechanics, Wave Motion and Heat
paras: Vectors, rectilinear motion, plane motion, dynamics of particles, work and energy, linear momentum, rotational motion, statics, angular momentum, harmonic motion, gravitation, wave motion, sound waves, temperature, heat, first and second laws of thermodynamics, kinetic theory of gases.
3 lectures, 3 hours laboratory.

courses.label: PHYS 200
courses.title: General Physics If
paras: Electromagnetism, A.C. circuits, geometrical and physical optics, introduction to atomic and nuclear physics. 3 lectures, 3 hours laboratory.

courses.label: PHYS 232
courses.title: Electricity and Magnetism
paras: Electrostatics, magnetic fields, electromagnetic induction, alternating current theory, the development of Maxwell’s equations. 2 lectures, 3 hours laboratory and one hour problems on alternate weeks.
Note: Students in Honours Physics take 3 hours laboratory or problems weekly.

courses.label: PHYS 233
courses.title: Laboratory
paras: Selected experiments in electricity and magnetism, optics, electronics and structure of solids. 6 hours per week.

courses.label: PHYS 235
courses.title: Optics
paras: An elementary course in geometrical and physical optics. Refraction ,and reflection at plane and curved surfaces; thin and thick lenses; optical instruments. The wave nature of light; interference; diffraction; slits and gratings, resolution. Polarization; optical activity; photometry.
2 lectures, 3 hours laboratory.
Note: Students enrolled in the Chemistry and the Chemistry and Physics courses take laboratory work in alternate weeks.

courses.label: PHYS 236
courses.title: Physical Optics
paras: The wave nature of light; interference, diffraction, slits and gratings, resolution. Polarization, optical activity, photometry. 3 lectures, 3 hours laboratory alternate weeks, one term.

courses.label: PHYS 237
courses.title: Astronomy I
paras: A survey course in astronomy. Aspects of the sky; motions of the earth; the earth and the moon; the solar system; gravitational astronomy; the sun; the stars; stellar motions; comets; meteors; meteorites; interstellar matter; the structure of the galaxy; exterior systems; cosmogony; radio astronomy.
3 lectures.

courses.label: PHYS 242
courses.title: Electricity and Magnetism
paras: Electrostatics, D.C. circuits, magnetic fields, electromagnetic induction, A.C. circuits, electrical measurements, introductory electronics.
2 lectures, 3 hours laboratory and 2 hours problems on alternate weeks.

courses.label: PHYS 243
courses.title: Electricity and Magnetism
paras: Electrostatics, D.C. circuits, magnetic fields, electromagnetic induction, A.C. circuits, electrical measurements. 3 lectures, 3 hours laboratory alternate weeks, one term.

courses.label: PHYS 245
courses.title: Structure of Solids
paras: Electronic structure of atoms and atomic bonding, crystal structure and space lattices, symmetry, crystal geometry, stereographic projections, theory of X-ray diffraction, X-ray methods, crystal formation, crystal defects, physical properties of crystals.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: PHYS 331
courses.title: Classical Mechanics I
paras: Foundations of Newtonian mechanics. Dynamics of a particle; harmonic oscillator; central force motion; conservative force; potential energy. Dynamics of a system of particles; conservation laws; translation and fixed-axis rotation of a rigid body. Moving frames of reference. Lagrange’s equations.
3 lectures.
Department of Physics

courses.label: PHYS 332
courses.title: Electronics
paras: A survey of electronic circuits. Basic A.C. circuit theory; rectifiers and filter circuits; triode, pentode and transistor amplifiers; equivalent circuits; feedback and oscillators; regulations; electronic measuring devices; pulse circuits.
2 lectures, 3 hours laboratory alternate weeks for students not taking Physics 333.

courses.label: PHYS 333
courses.title: Intermediate Laboratory
paras: Selected experiments in mechanics, heat, sound, optics, spectroscopy, X-ray, atomic physics, electricity, magnetism, and electronics.
6 hours laboratory.

courses.label: PHYS 334
courses.title: Atomic and Nuclear Physics I
paras: Special theory of relativity, growth of atomic concepts, quantum theory of thermal radiation, particle aspects of electromagnetic radiations. Rutherford atom, Bohr atom, wave aspects of particles, wave mechanics, solution of Schroedinger’s equation, one-electron atoms.
3 lectures.

courses.label: PHYS 335
courses.title: Thermodynamics, Kinetic Theory of Gases, Statistical Mechanics
paras: Fundamental principles of thermodynamics, kinetic theory, and statistical mechanics. Thermodynamic systems, equations of state, work, first and second laws of thermodynamics, change of phase, entropy, kinetic theory of an ideal gas, distribution of molecular velocities, transport phenomena, Maxwell-Boltzmann statistics, quantum statistics, fluctuations.
3 lectures.

courses.label: PHYS 336
courses.title: Physical Mathematics I
paras: Vector analysis; vector differential operators and associated integral theorems. Introduction to tensors. Curvilinear co-ordinate systems. Partial differential equations of mathematical physics; Laplace’s, wave and diffusion equations; Legendre and Bessel functions. Fourier analysis; eigenfunctions.
2 lectures.

courses.label: PHYS 337
courses.title: Astronomy II
paras: Selected topics in astrophysics, cosmogony, and radioastronomy. 2 lectures.

courses.label: PHYS 338
courses.title: Geophysics I
paras: An introductory course on the physics of the Earth. Origin, heat and temperature of the Earth, study of earthquakes and the Earth’s interior through earthquake waves; gravity and isostasy; terrestrial magnetism; effects of heat, temperature and strain on rocks; origins of continents, mountain ranges, the ocean floors, meteorology; geophysical techniques.

courses.label: PHYS 339
courses.title: Atomic and Nuclear Physics
paras: Fundamentals of modern physics; special theory of relativity, quantization of electromagnetic radiation, wave properties of particles, the hydrogen atom, atomic and X-ray spectra, nuclear structure, nuclear reactions, molecular and solid state physics.
. 3 lectures..

courses.label: PHYS 340
courses.title: Quantum Physics I
paras: The origins of quantum theory. Planck’s radiation law, photo-electric and Compton effects, the nuclear atom and Bohr model.
wave-particle experiments. Schroedinger equation. Solutions for potential barriers and wells. 3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: PHYS 341A
courses.title: Electronics I
paras: An integrated survey of tube and transistor circuits. Basic A.C. circuit theory, passive components, simple power supplies, amplifiers using equivalent circuit analysis techniques, oscillators.
3 lectures, 3 hours laboratory, one term.

courses.label: PHYS 341B
courses.title: Electronics II
paras: A continuation of Electronics I covering feedback, regulated power supplies, pulse circuitry, servosystems, electrical analogies and a variety of special purpose circuits.
2 lectures, one term.

courses.label: PHYS 344
courses.title: Nuclear Physics
paras: Sizes and masses of nuclei and their determination. Models of nuclear structure. Nuclear decay and reactions. Detectors and accelerators. Elementary particles.
2 lectures, one term.

courses.label: PHYS 431
courses.title: Classical Mechanics II
paras: Review of Lagrangian formulation of mechanics. Rotation of a rigid body; the inertia tensor; Hamilton’s principle; Hamilton’s equations. Classical theory of small vibrations. Dynamics of deformable matter; elasticity; hydrodynamics.
2 lectures.

courses.label: PHYS 432
courses.title: Physics of Solid State Devices
paras: Review of vacuum tube electronics, statistics of electrons in semiconductors, transport properties, minority carrier injection, theory of pn junctions, transistors, tunnel diodes, field effect devices: applications.
3 hours per week, second term.

courses.label: PHYS 433
courses.title: Advanced Laboratory
paras: Selected experiments in atomic and nuclear physics, solid state physics, thermodynamics; electrical and electronic measurements; vacuum techniques. In addition. a short research problem will be assigned.
3. 6 or 9 hours laboratory.

courses.label: PHYS 434
courses.title: Atomic and Nuclear Physics II
paras: Multi-electron atoms: identical particles and the Pauli principle, the helium atom, Hartree theory of multi-electron atoms, the periodic table, the vector model. Nuclear physics: particle acceleration and detection, nuclear structure, the decay of unstable nuclei, nuclear reactions, elementary particles.
2 lectures.

courses.label: PHYS 435
courses.title: Solid State Physics
paras: Atomic bonding; crystal structure and space lattices; symmetry; crystal geometry; defects; physical properties of crystals; free electron theory of metals: band theory: properties of semiconductors and insulators.
3 hours per week. first term.
Department of Physics

courses.label: PHYS 436
courses.title: Physical Mathematics II
paras: Theory of functions of a complex variable; conformal mapping and applications. Boundary value problems on linear partial differential equations; separation of variables; Green’s functions. Linear integral equations. Integral transforms (Laplace, Fourier).
3 lectures.

courses.label: PHYS 437
courses.title: Topics in Theoretical Physics
paras: Selected subjects for advanced study by theoretically inclined students; topics in relativistic, quantum, and statistical physics.
3 hours per week, second term.

Graduate Course Descriptions

courses.label: PHYS 620
courses.title: Quantum Mechanics I
paras: Principles of wave mechanics. Schroedinger’s equation. One dimensional and spherically symmetric problems. Matrix mechanics. Angular momentum. Time independent and time dependent approximation methods.
Three lectures, first term.

courses.label: PHYS 621
courses.title: Quantum Mechanics II
paras: Semi-classical treatment of radiation. Identical particles and spin. Atoms and molecules. Scattering. Dirac equation. Quantization of the electromagentic field. Low order radiation processes. . Three lectures, second term.

courses.label: PHYS 622
courses.title: Group Theory and Quantum Mechanics
paras: Introduction to group theory; groups, representations of groups, character tables. Group theory and quantum mechanics, the permutation and rotation groups. Applications of the theory to atomic spectra, the theory of angular momentum, molecular symmetry and solid state physics.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: PHYS 623
courses.title: Advanced Quantum Mechanics
paras: Dirac theory; the single particle description of relativistic quantum mechanics; bound state and scattering problems— the need for a many-particle (field) approach. Classical relativistic field theory, Feynman-Schwinger quantization of this theory. The radiation field, the electron field. Interaction of these fields. The S-matrix; Compton scattering, Coulomb scattering. The magnetic moment of the electron, the Lamb shift. Renormalization.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: PHYS 627
courses.title: Atomic Spectra
paras: The fine and hyperfine structure of one-electron and many-electron atoms, the Zeeman and Stark effects. 3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: PHYS 628
courses.title: Molecular Spectra
paras: The electronic, vibrational, and rotational spectra of diatomic and polyatomic molecules and the Raman effect. 3 lectures, one term.
Department of Physics

courses.label: PHYS 630
courses.title: Nuclear Physics
paras: Fundamental properties of nuclei; internucleon forces, size, moments, shapes, binding energies. Nuclear models. Electromagnetic properties of nuclei. Particle radioactivity. Nuclear reactions.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: PHYS 634
courses.title: Advanced Classical Mechanics
paras: Review of elementary mechanics, Lagrangian formulation, variational principles, Hamiltonian formulations; rigid body kinematics and dynamics, special relativity, transformation theory, Hamilton-Jacobi theory.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: PHYS 635
courses.title: Electromagnetic Theory I
paras: The electrostatic and the magnetic field; energy, force and momentum relations in the electromagnetic field; Maxwell’s equations, solutions of the wave equation; radiation.
3 lectures, first term.

courses.label: PHYS 636
courses.title: Electromagnetic Theory II
paras: The special theory of relativity; the electromagnetic tensor; the field of moving charges; magnetohydrodynamics; selected topics.
3 lectures, second term.

courses.label: PHYS 640
courses.title: Electron Optics and Electron Microscopy
paras: Electrons in electrostatic fields, the electrostatic lens, the magnetic lens, aberrations, the electron microscope, theory of image contrast, Fresnel diffraction and image contour phenomena, electron diffraction and dark-field microscopy, experimental methods in electron microscopy.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: PHYS 641
courses.title: Electron Diffraction
paras: General theory of the diffraction of waves by crystals, experimental technique of electron diffraction, kinematic theory and interpretation of electron diffraction, patterns, refraction of electron waves, atomic scattering, dynamical theory, electron interference effects in electron microscope images.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: PHYS 645
courses.title: Statistical Mechanics
paras: Review of essential classical and quantum mechanics; microcanonical, canonical and grand canonical ensembles; quantum statistical mechanics, theory of the density matrix; fluctuations, noise, irreversible thermodynamics; transport theory; application to gases, liquids, solids.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: PHYS 647
courses.title: Low Temperature Physics
paras: Production and measurement of very low temperatures. Low temperature materials and techniques. Thermal, magnetic and electrical properties of matter at very low temperatures. Superconductivity. Liquid Hellium.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: PHYS 650
courses.title: Solid State Physics
paras: An introductory undergraduate course in classical solid state physics, or equivalent, is assumed. The free electron model in metals, band theory of solids, application of Brillouin zone theory, semiconductors, optical properties of solids and devices of current interest are some of the topics which are covered.
Three lectures, second term.

courses.label: PHYS 651
courses.title: Imperfections in Crystals
paras: Perfect and imperfect crystals, general properties and origins of point defects and dislocations, stacking faults, interactions of imperfections, influence of lattice imperfections on physical properties and their role in deformation of crystals and phase transformations, experimental detection and observation of imperfections.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: PHYS 652
courses.title: Photoconductivity and Luminescence
paras: Electron processes in crystals, photoconductive processes. Electrode effects, imperfection and energy band transitions, scattering, traps and trapping effects. Recombination kinetics, luminescence. Experimental methods and analysis.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: PHYS 653
courses.title: Inert Gas Solids
paras: Theory of crystal lattices: quantum mechanical basis, interatomic potentials, stability, dynamics of cubic close-packed lattices, thermodynamics of ideal crystals. anharmonicity. Experimental properties.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: PHYS 654
courses.title: Advanced Quantum Theory of Solids
paras: Theoretical and experimental techniques for determination of the band structure of metals and semiconductors; electrical and thermal conduction processes and electron-lattice interactions.
3 lectures, one term.
Department of Physics

courses.label: PHYS 655
courses.title: Optical Properties of Semiconductors
paras: Refiection and refraction of electromagnetic waves at dielectric and conducting interfaces. Dispersion, absorption processes, photo effects, magneto-optical effects, emission of radiation.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: PHYS 656
courses.title: Magnetism
paras: Introduction to the theory of magnetic phenomena in metals and non-metals. Relevant experimental work will also be discussed. 3 hours per week, one term.

courses.label: PHYS 660
courses.title: Selected Topics in Physics
paras: 3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: PHYS 667
courses.title: Molecular Biology
paras: Selected topics of interest to biologists, biochemists and biophysicists will be presented at the advanced level with the aim of evaluating recent work and development in each area. Each will be developed from basic concepts and interrelationships emphasized. Topics will include: the structure of proteins and their properties in solution, transport through biological membranes, cell morphology and physiology, structure and function of selected organells, biosynthesis of macromolecules, and the chemistry of enzyme action. This graduate course is to be presented by members of the Biology, Chemistry, and Physics Departments and is intended to cover those areas common to these disciplines (identical to Biology 667 and Chemistry 667).

courses.label: PHYS 670
courses.title: Physics of the Earth’s Interior
paras: Selected topics in theoretical geophysics; seismology, rheology of the Earth, geomagnetism, the Earth’s rotation. 3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: PHYS 675
courses.title: General Relativity and Cosmology
paras: Tensor analysis: covariant and contravariant tensors, covariant differentation. Riemmanian space, geodesics. Ricci tensor, Christoffel symbols. General relativity: gravitation and special relativity, equivalence principle, field equations of general relativity, Schwarzchild- metric, observational evidence for the general theory. Cosmology: Newtonian, Einstein and de Sitter universes, the expanding universe, cosmological principle and steady-state universe, observational clues.
3 lectures, one term.

courses.label: PHYS 680
courses.title: Galactic Structure
paras: Introduction to statistical theory and distribuion laws. Statistical description of the galactic system. Stellar motions in the vicinity of the sun. Space distribution of stars. Galactic rotation.
3 lectures and discussion, one term.

Notes: (1) Students electing an Honours Programme or a Major in Political Science, or an Honours Programme in such related subjects as History, Economics, Sociology or Psychology are encouraged to register in Political Science 110 in their first year. Other students are encouraged to register in Political Science 100. Either of these courses will serve as a prerequisite for senior courses in Political Science.

(2) Courses designated “Full course, ‘half year” are comparable to a normal year course in their content. They are, however, offered, on a more concentrated basis during one term only. In drawing up a programme a student would regard such a course as two courses during the term in which it is offered and would combine it with another such course, or two half-courses during the remaining term. The advantage of such a combination of courses is that it allows a more concentrated study of a more limited number of subjects at any given time.
(3) The number of hours or lectures shown after the course description is an attempt to indicate the “normal”; each instructor determines how often his particular class will meet.

courses.label: PHYS 15
courses.title: Government and Politics
paras: An introduction to liberal democratic ideals and a comparative treatment of the institutions and practices of modern democratic government with particular reference to Canada, the United States and Great Britain. Note: This course is restricted to students in the Co-operative Engineering programme.

courses.label: PHYS 100
courses.title: Introduction to Political Science
paras: A study of the origin, nature and impact of contemporary political doctrines including Communism, Fascism, Democratic Socialism and Democratic Capitalism, together with a study of the institutions and practices of modern government, with particular reference to the governments of Canada, the United States and Great Britain.
3 lectures.

courses.label: PHYS 101
courses.title: Introductory Politics
paras: (a) A study of some of the leading political ideas of the contemporary world. (b) A comparative treatment of the institutions and practices of modern government with particular reference to Canada. Note: This course is restricted to students in the Co-operative Mathematics programme. Parts (a) and (b) will be offered in alternate terms.

courses.label: PHYS 110
courses.title: Democratic Government
paras: An examination of the theory and practice of constitutional democracy in modern industrial “mass” society. The relationship between basic political objectives and general features of organization.
procedure and practice will be emphasized, with primary reference to Canada Great Britain and the United States. Full course. 3 lectures.

courses.label: PSCI 250
courses.title: The History of Political Theory
paras: An examination of the theories of some of the major figures in the history of western political thought, from ancient Greece to the present day.
3 lectures.
261.* Contemporary International Politics. A study of the main political developments and issues in the relations of nations since World War II. 3 lectures. Fall term only.

courses.label: PSCI 270
courses.title: Public Administration
paras: A comparative analysis of the public services of the major democracies with particular reference to the legal basis, organization and political and judicial control of the administrative processes.
3 lectures.

courses.label: PSCI 280
courses.title: Canadian Government and Politics
paras: A critical examination of the structure of Canadian government and politics. 3 lectures.

courses.label: PSCI 281
courses.title: American Government and Politics
paras: The theory and practice of American government and politics at the federal and state levels. Full course, half year. Fall term only.

courses.label: PSCI 282
courses.title: British Government and Politics
paras: A critical examination of the theory and practice of government and politics in Great Britain. Full course, half year. Winter term only.
283.* The Dynamics of Soviet Politics. A survey of both the theoretical and practical aspects of political life in the Soviet Union, emphasizing Soviet domestic politics and political institutions.
3 lectures. Fall term only.
284.* Government and Politics in Western Europe. A comparative study of the government and politics of France, Italy and the Federal German Republic in the post-war world.
3 lectures. Winter term only.
363.* The Soviet Union and the World. An analysis of Soviet foreign policy and the international communist movement, with particular emphasis upon the Sino-Soviet conflict.
Prerequisite: Political Science 283 or 261.
3 lectures. Winter term only.

courses.label: PSCI 364
courses.title: Theory and Practice of International Relations
paras: An examination of the concepts of international relations and the study of International Relations as a discipline. A treatment of foreign policy analysis with special emphasis on components of national power and methods and trends in the pursuit of national and collective interests.

3 lectures.

392.* Interest Group Politics. A study of interest group theory and comparative analysis of the internal politics of interest groups and their role in the political process.
3 lectures. Winter term only. Admission by consent of instructor.
393.* Voting Behaviour. A comparative study of the bases of electoral choice in Canada, Great Britain and the United States. 3 lectures. Winter term only. Admission by consent of instructor.

3 lectures.

courses.label: PSYCH 110
courses.title: Introductory Psychology
paras: This course is designed to provide the students with an understanding of the basic concepts and techniques of modern psychology as a behavioural science. 3 lectures.

courses.label: PSYCH 111
courses.title: Introductory Psychology I

courses.label: PSYCH 112

paras: (For Co-operative Mathematics students only.)

3 lectures.

courses.label: PSYCH 150
courses.title: Experimental Methods in Psychology
paras: An introduction to experimental methods in psychology. In respect to content, emphasis will be placed on the fields of learning, perception, and physiological psychology. (For students in Honours Psychology and Honours Biology and Psychology. Other students by permission of Department only.)
2 lectures, 2 hours laboratory.

courses.label: PSYCH 200
courses.title: General Experimental Psychology
paras: An introduction to the methods of experimental psychology. Laboratory experience will be used to introduce the student to the data and theories of learning and perception. courses.label: PSYCH 280
courses.title: Statistical Methods in Psychology
paras: An introduction to the logical and theoretical bases of the application of statistical methods to the solution of problems in the social sciences. 2 lectures, 1 hour laboratory.

courses.label: PSYCH 290
courses.title: Principles of Learning
paras: This course is designed to introduce the student to learning theory and to provide an understanding of experimental techniques in this area. Required of all Honours Psychology students.
2 lectures, 2 hour laboratory.

courses.title: Social Psychology
paras: In this course the student will study socialization, social perception, interaction within and between groups, and the communication process.
3 lectures.

3 lectures, winter term.

courses.label: PSYCH 360
courses.title: Sensation and Perception
paras: The characteristics of sensation and perception will be studied in relation to the physics of the stimuli and physiology of the sensory apparatus. Required of all Honours Psychology students.
2 lectures, 2 hours laboratory.

courses.label: PSYCH 370
courses.title: Animal Learning
paras: More advanced study of learning principles, together with a presentation of, and practice in, the techniques of experiments with animals.
2 hours lectures, 2 hours laboratory.

courses.label: PSYCH 380
courses.title: Advanced Physiological Psychology
paras: More advanced study of the physiological basis of behaviour, with particular reference to the functioning of the nervous system.
Prerequisite: 252.
2 hours lectures, 2 hours laboratory.

courses.label: PSYCH 390
courses.title: Motivation and Emotion
paras: Past experience, the social environment, and physiological responses as determinants of motivated behaviour. Prerequisite: 290.
2 hours lectures, 2 hours laboratory.

courses.label: PSYCH 410
courses.title: History and Systems
paras: An examination of current theoretical approaches to psychological problems presented in a historical context. 3 hours lectures.

courses.label: PSYCH 430
courses.title: Problems in Contemporary Psychology
paras: Conducted, for the most part, as a seminar class, the purpose of this course will be to examine the latest developments in psychology, chiefly through journal publications, in order to evaluate contemporary trends in research and theory.
2 lectures.

courses.label: PSYCH 611
courses.title: Human Factors Engineering I
paras: The human being as an element in an engineering system; his physical and mental capabilities and limitations; his assets and liabilities as compared to automatic elements; his physical and mental requirements for optimum functioning as an element in a system.

courses.label: PSYCH 612
courses.title: Human Factors Engineering I
paras: More advanced study of selected problems presented in Psychology 611, together with laboratory demonstrations.

courses.label: PSYCH 621
courses.title: Introduction to Clinical Psychology
paras: A critical evaluation of concepts and principles of particular concern to the clinical psychologist. The course will include historical developments, ethical problems, and role definition. Practicum involves presentation of clinical test materials with lectures pertaining to the development and reliability of, and the validation research on, each test.
Department of Psychology

courses.title: Psychodynamics
paras: This course deals with the theoretical structures upon which psychological treatment is based. Coverage ranges from orthodox psychoanalytic theory to current phenomonological and social-learning theories. Practicum work includes supervised examinations of school children on standard measures of intelligence and report writing.

courses.title: Personality Assessment
paras: This course deals with the nature, validity, and underlying assumptions of the major “diagnostic” clinical tests. Emphasis is placed on the more difficult “projective” tests. Practicum work includes discussion and interpretation of protocols secured from hospital and reformatory populations.

courses.label: PSYCH 624
courses.title: Psychopathology
paras: Course materials concern orientations to psychopathology, problems in current approaches, and suggestions for other theoretical systems. Practicum work involves collection of clinical data in a clinical setting under supervision of staff persons.

courses.label: PSYCH 625
courses.title: Psychotherapy
paras: A detailed coverage of psychotherapeutic systems and theories of personality change and of related research.

courses.label: PSYCH 626
courses.title: Psychotherapy practicum
paras: Students will conduct continuing psychotherapy under supervision of the staff. Theoretical and practical issues will be discussed.

courses.label: PSYCH 627
courses.title: Seminar in Clinical Psychology I
paras: This seminar is designed to enable individual staff members to present their current points of view and research contributions.

courses.label: PSYCH 628
courses.title: Seminar in Clinical Psychology II
paras: Presentations by individual staff members supplementary to those given in 627.

courses.label: PSYCH 629
courses.title: Group Psychotherapy
paras: A study of the underlying principles of group therapy with emphasis on the psychodynamics of the individual as he operates in a group situation.

courses.label: PSYCH 630
courses.title: Directed Study
paras: This course offers an opportunity for students who have previously taken a half-year course in a specific area to explore selected problems in greater depth.

courses.label: PSYCH 631
courses.title: Advanced Statistics
paras: An advanced introduction to descriptive statistics and statistical inference. Prerequisite: Psychology 280 or its equivalent.

paras: ization and modal as well as deviant personality types. Differential processes

of socialization, and the effects of personality types on social organization. Social structures considered will include occupational, fraternal, and kinship groupings. 3 lectures.

courses.label: SOC 230
courses.title: Family and Kinship
paras: An evaluation of the origin and growth of the family as a social institution; its structures and functions in primitive and modern societies; the effect of modern technology on the family; trends and contemporary problems.
3 lectures.

courses.label: SOC 240
courses.title: Collective Behaviour
paras: The sociological analysis of the behaviour of crowds, mobs, publics, and related phenomena and their relationships to social organization and social change.
3 lectures.

courses.label: SOC 241
courses.title: Social Movements
paras: The sociological analysis of varieties of social movements and their relationships to social organization and social change. 3 lectures.

courses.label: SOC 250
courses.title: Crime and Society
paras: An analysis and criticism of the major theories of criminal behaviour. Emphasis is given to the relationship between social structure and criminal behaviour; types of criminal behaviour such as drug addiction; statistics and contemporary research. A sound knowledge of sociological concepts is advisable.
3 lectures.

courses.label: SOC 251
courses.title: Ethnic and Racial Relations
paras: Relations between different racial and cultural groups; analysis of majority-minority group status. 3 lectures.

courses.label: SOC 252
courses.title: Juvenile Delinquency
paras: A systematic analysis and criticism is presented of biological, psychological, psychoanalytical and sociological theories of juvenile delinquency. Attention is given to statistics and contemporary research with special emphasis on the distribution and types of delinquent subcultures. Students should possess a sound knowledge of basic sociological concepts.
3 lectures.
260%. Population. The study of population as an area of sociological investigation; population size, composition, and distribution; population trends and problems. 3 lectures.

courses.label: SOC 270
courses.title: Communication
paras: An analysis of the role of language and other symbol systems in social interaction; the interplay between communication and the social system; the formation of attitudes through language; social and individual disorders as caused by, and reflected in, the breakdown in the communication process.
3 lectures.

courses.label: SOC 300
courses.title: Human Communities
paras: A comparative analysis of different types of human communities from mainly sociological and anthropological points of view: primary emphasis on types of communities found in non-literate, folk, and pre-industrial societies; major theories concerning communities of these
types. 3 lectures.

courses.label: SOC 301
courses.title: Urban Sociology
paras: The comparative study of urbanization as a process; the culture and social organization of cities, urban problems; special attention is given to industrial cities of Western societies.
3 lectures.

courses.label: SOC 315
courses.title: Social Stratification
paras: Analysis of social classes in society including their bases for development, composition, and consequences for society. 3 lectures.

courses.label: SOC 320
courses.title: Sociological Research
paras: A systematic treatment of the logic and practice of methods basic to social research. Examination of problems of experimental design, sampling, data gathering, and analysis in the context of case studies of research. Students will be given laboratory experience in several techniques of research.
3 lectures.

courses.label: SOC 325
courses.title: Sociological Theory
paras: Major European and American sociologists and “schools” from Comte to the present. Emphasis will be less on history and biography than on the ideas, and their application to an understanding of major issues generated in human societies.
3 lectures.

courses.label: SOC 331
courses.title: Social Change. A systematic review and analysis of major theories of
paras: social change with particular attention to evolutionism, historicism and functionalism. Theoretical problems are then examined within a specific context, such as social organization, social stratification, economic institutions, urban structures, etc.
3 lectures.

courses.label: SOC 335
courses.title: Sociology of Science
paras: The study of science as an institution; its historical development and contemporary relationships with other institutions including government, education, and industry.
3 lectures.

courses.label: SOC 339
courses.title: Industrial Sociology
paras: Sociological analysis of industry, including relationships between labour and management and industry and society. 3 lectures.

courses.label: SOC 340
courses.title: Formal Organizations. A survey of theory and research on formal
paras: organizations making use of selected contributions from the scientific management and human relations approaches, but with emphasis on the structure and functions of large scale organizations. The nature and types of formal organizations; control techniques and leadership; relations of the organization to its
Department of Sociology and Anthropology
clients and publics; informal aspects of the organization; organizational tensions and pathologies of bureaucratic systems; how the organization adjusts to change. 3 lectures.

courses.label: SOC 341
courses.title: Sociology of Occupations
paras: The sociological study of occupations as an aid to understanding the social structure; social and demographic aspects of the labour force; the meaning of work; the relation of work and leisure; career and occupational mobility patterns; occupation and status; professionalization; trends in occupations.
3 lectures.

courses.label: SOC 355
courses.title: Sociology of Religion
paras: The analysis of religion as a social institution; its relationship to culture, personality and social change with consideration given to theories of religious behaviour and contemporary research findings.
3 lectures.

courses.label: SOC 360
courses.title: Political Sociology. The sociological analysis of the institutionalization
paras: of power, political movements, parties, conflict and its accommodation. 3 lectures.

courses.label: SOC 365
courses.title: Social Structure of the Soviet Union
paras: A sociological analysis of contemporary Soviet society focusing on the patterns and functions of its basic institutions including the family, government, education, and industry; consideration of class formation and distribution of power.
3 lectures.

courses.label: SOC 380
courses.title: Sociology of Health and Welfare
paras: The structure and processes of health and welfare services are examined as parts of the institutional network of North American society. Professionalization and bureaucratic organization as aids and obstacles toward institutionalized goals. The impact of scientific and technological changes on the structure of health and welfare services and careers.
3 lectures.

courses.label: SOC 385
courses.title: Education and Society
paras: The structure and processes of education are examined in relation to those of community and society. Schools as sources, recipients, and modifiers, and professionalization of personnel in relation to the institutionalized goals of education in North American society.
3 lectures.

courses.label: SOC 450
courses.title: Seminar: Problems in Contemporary Theory and Research
paras: Examination of current frames of reference and theories in sociology and related disciplines. Their utility in sociological problem formulation and their test by current methods and techniques.
1-3 hours.

courses.label: SOC 465
courses.title: Readings
paras: Selected readings and essay assignments under the direction of a staff member. 3-4 hours.

courses.label: SOC 470
courses.title: Seminar: Practicum in Theory and Methodology
paras: A preparation for advanced undergraduate students for an independent, sophisticated orientation to graduate study. The practicum provides opportunities for.
(1) developing research designs on the basis of extant theory, and
(2) theorizing on the basis of the reanalysis and reinterpretation of extant data. 1-3 hours.

courses.label: SOC 499
courses.title: Senior Honours Essay
paras: Required of all honours students in Sociology or Psychology — Sociology in their fourth year.

Undergraduate Course Descriptions
General Arts students who wish to major in Spanish will take Spanish 100, 200, 300 and any two Honours Spanish courses chosen in consultation with the department chairman.
Note: The number of hours or lectures shown after the course description is an attempt to indicate the “normal”; each instructor determines how often his particular class will meet.

courses.label: SPAN 1-50
courses.title: Introduction to Spanish
paras: Intensive drill in the fundamentals of grammar and composition. The language laboratory will be used regularly.
No prerequisite, though the student should have Grade XIII French.
5 lectures.
Department of Spanish and Italian

courses.label: SPAN 100
courses.title: Survey of Spanish Literature
paras: Intensive review of grammar and composition. Survey of Spanish literature. The language laboratory will be used regularly.
Prerequisite: Spanish 1-50 or Grade XIII Spanish.
4 lectures.

courses.label: SPAN 200
courses.title: Survey of the Spanish Novel
paras: For students in General Arts only. Critical survey of representative Spanish novels, from Lazarillo de Tormes to the midtwentieth century. Lectures, readings, reports.
Prerequisite: Spanish 100.
3 lectures.

courses.label: SPAN 210
courses.title: Spanish Civilization
paras: A study in English of the main historical and cultural currents in Spain and Spanish America. (Honours Spanish students may not take this course for credit.)
3 lectures.

courses.label: SPAN 250
courses.title: Advanced Composition and Conversation
paras: Phonetics, intensive study of grammar, oral practice, practice in the language laboratory.
Prerequisite: Spanish 100.
3 lectures.

courses.label: SPAN 260
courses.title: Prose and Drama of the 18th and 19th Centuries
paras: Critical reading of the principal authors and playwrights of the period. Lectures in Spanish, readings, reports.
Prerequisite: Spanish 100.
3 lectures.

courses.label: SPAN 300
courses.title: Survey of the Spanish Drama
paras: For students in General Arts only. Critical survey of representative Spanish plays, from Juan del Encina to the midtwentieth century. Lectures, readings, reports.
Prerequisite: Spanish 200.
3 lectures.

courses.label: SPAN 350
courses.title: Advanced Composition
paras: Writing of essays based on critical examination of selected plays and novels; discussion, in Spanish, of these works; practice in the language laboratory.
Prerequisite: Spanish 250.
2 lectures.

courses.label: SPAN 360
courses.title: Spanish Prose and Drama of the 16th and 17th Centuries
paras: Critical study of the literature of the Spanish Golden Age.
Prerequisite: Spanish 260.
2 lectures.

courses.label: SPAN 365
courses.title: The Realistic and Naturalistic Novel in Spain
paras: 2 hours.

courses.label: SPAN 370
courses.title: Survey of Spanish American Literature
paras: A critical study of Spanish American literature from the Cortés letters to the present.
Prerequisite: Spanish 100.
3 lectures.

courses.label: SPAN 375
courses.title: Individual Playwrights of the Golden Age
paras: 3 hours seminar.

courses.label: SPAN 450
courses.title: Senior Spanish Composition and Oral Practice
paras: The language laboratory will be used regularly.
Prerequisite: Spanish 350.
2 lectures.

courses.label: SPAN 455
courses.title: Individual Writers of the Twentieth Century
paras: 3 hours seminar.

courses.label: SPAN 460
courses.title: Spanish Literature of the 20th Century
paras: Critical examination of the works of the most significant writers of this Century.
Prerequisite: Spanish 360.
2 lectures.

courses.label: SPAN 465
courses.title: Cervantes and His Age
paras: 3 lectures.

courses.label: SPAN 470
courses.title: Mediaeval Spanish
paras: Study of the literature from the beginnings to 1500 A.D.; introduction to Old Spanish grammar; elementary Portuguese. Prerequisite: Spanish 370.
2 lectures.

courses.label: SPAN 475
courses.title: The Modernista Movement
paras: 3 lectures.

courses.label: SPAN 476
courses.title: The Novel in Mexico
paras: 3 lectures.

courses.label: SPAN 480
courses.title: Survey of Spanish Poetry
paras: From the Poema del Cid to the present. Lectures, reports.
Prerequisite: Spanish 300 or 360.
2 lectures.
